correctness.rationale: Every nonzero proper ideal is indexed by a nonempty proper support \(S\subsetneq[r]\), and adjacency is exactly \(S\cap T\ne\varnothing\). The incidence matrix \(B\) has rank \(r\) because the singleton-support columns are the standard basis; therefore \(B^\mathsf{T}B\) is a rank-\(r\) real symmetric pattern matrix with off-diagonal entry \(|S\cap T|\), giving \(M\ge(2^r-2)-r\). Independently replaying the stated white family \(\{1,2\},\{2,\ldots,r\},\ldots,\{r\}\) gives exactly \(r\) successive forces, hence \(Z\le(2^r-2)-r\). The standard inequality \(M\le Z\) closes both bounds and yields \(\operatorname{mr}=r\). A fresh rational reconstruction in this audit reproduced ranks and forcing sizes for \(r=3,4,5\); those finite checks are corroborative only.
correctness.risk: The minimum-rank statement is over the real symmetric pattern model; characteristic-dependent minimum rank is not claimed.
sources: AIM Minimum Rank--Special Graphs Work Group, DOI:10.1016/j.laa.2007.10.009

final_claim: For \(R=F_1\times\cdots\times F_r\), a product of \(r\ge3\) fields, the intersection graph of nonzero proper ideals has real symmetric minimum rank \(r\), maximum nullity and zero forcing number \(2^r-r-2\), with the explicit \(r\)-white-vertex forcing construction stated in the package.
limitations: Products of at least three fields only; the two-field graph is two isolated vertices.
